notes: Johnson-Fulton & Watson place C. tetraporum outside core Cochlospermum and, in the relevant topology summary, sister to monophyletic Amoreuxia. Flora Neotropica morphology gives one continuous filament/anther range rather than the two discrete fertile-stamen sets of Amoreuxia. Searches under C. tetraporum, C. argentinense, Maximilianea tetrapora, and M. argentinensis recovered no species-level flower-visitation or effective-pollination source, so the nearest candidate remains OPEN.

The 2009 species-level reproductive-biology study reports about 160 fertile poricidal anthers and predominant pollination by solitary Centris bees. The phylogeny places C. orinocense outside core Cochlospermum, but the closer C. tetraporum candidate remains eligibility-OPEN, so C. orinocense cannot be promoted merely because its pollination evidence is stronger.

Core Cochlospermum retains the ancestral uniform-stamen state. Roubik et al. 1982 directly identify Centris as the most important pollinators of C. vitifolium. This high-quality ecological evidence does not override the preregistered phylogenetic-distance priority while the closer C. tetraporum eligibility gate is unresolved.
